title: Company-wide policies and processes (Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, Travel, Templates)
author: Priya Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and approved internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, managers, and partners responsible for operational compliance and day-to-day execution.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with network or data access.
- Covers corporate systems (G Suite/Workspace, identity provider, expense system), production and non-production infrastructure, and procurement/contract activities.
- Does not replace team-level runbooks and service-specific policies; such documents must be linked and kept consistent with this policy.

1) Roles and ownership

| Role | Responsibility | Primary contact |
|------|----------------|----------------|
| People Ops | Hiring, onboarding, travel & expense approval policies, employee lifecycle | people-ops@redwood.ai |
| Security | IAM policy, privileged access review, vendor security assessments | security@redwood.ai |
| Finance | Procurement thresholds, vendor contract sign-off, expense reimbursements | finance@redwood.ai |
| IT/Platform | System-level access provisioning, privileged access monitoring, change windows | infra-ops@redwood.ai |
| Team owners | Service-level changes, runbooks, production rollouts | (see service owner directory) |

2) Access & permissions

Objective: enforce least privilege, auditable approvals, and timely lifecycle management for all user and service access.

Access types and rules:
- Human user access: provisioned via the identity provider (Okta/GCP IAM/Azure AD). All users must authenticate with SSO + MFA.
- Service accounts: limited to specific scopes; keys rotate at least every 90 days unless scoped short-lived credentials are used.
- Privileged/Admin access: requires approval from People Ops and Security; time-limited elevated access (just-in-time) preferred.

Onboarding and offboarding (procedures):
1. Hiring offer accepted -> People Ops creates employee record and submits provisioning request to IT (via /templates/access-request).
2. IT provisions base access (email, laptop, corporate network) within 1 business day for US/EU hires, 2 business days for APAC hires.
3. Manager requests additional system access (Jira, GitHub, GCP projects) using the Access Request template; approvals required from manager and Data/Service owner.
4. Offboarding: Manager files termination task in People Ops; IT revokes SSO and access within 4 hours of offboarding for terminated accounts.

Access reviews and attestations:
- Quarterly automated entitlement reports (Security) with team owner attestation due within 10 business days.
- Emergency access (Break Glass) process: documented justification + Security post-facto review within 48 hours.

3) Change management

Purpose: reduce operational risk while enabling fast iteration. All changes that impact production services must follow the change model below.

Change categories:
- Standard Changes: low-risk routine changes pre-approved by Change Board (e.g., certificate renewals).
- Minor Changes: code/config changes with no customer-visible impact; require automated tests and one approver from the owning team.
- Major Changes: schema migrations, deploys with potential downtime, infrastructure changes that modify networking/permissions; require a Change Request (CR), risk assessment, test plan, and CAB approval.

Change request process (high level):
1. Create CR in the Change Management system with: description, risk assessment, rollback plan, test plan, scheduled window, and owners.
2. Automated validation runs: CI, canary checks, pre-deployment smoke tests.
3. Approval: Minor/Standard changes approved by team owner; Major changes require CAB signoff (Security, SRE, Product, Finance as applicable).
4. Scheduling: Prefer weekly change windows (Tuesday & Thursday 02:00–06:00 UTC) unless emergency.
5. Post-change verification: owner runs verification checklist within 60 minutes and updates CR.
6. Rollback: follow documented rollback runbook in case SLO or health checks fail. Post-change review required for Major changes.

Emergency changes:
- Emergency changes must be labeled in the CR system and accompanied by post-incident review within 7 days. Emergency changes should be minimized and retroactively evaluated.

4) Data management

Data classification:
- Public: information safe for public disclosure.
- Internal: operational data not for public sharing.
- Confidential: customer data, PII, or otherwise regulated data.
- Restricted: regulated or highly sensitive data (e.g., health, payment data) — requires additional controls and potential Restricted confidentiality.

Handling rules by classification:
- Encryption: All Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest (KMS/HSM managed keys) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Access: RBAC and Just-In-Time access for Confidential/Restricted datasets; data access audits every 30 days.
- Storage: Use approved storage systems (see table below).

| Data type | Approved storage | Retention default |
|-----------|------------------|-------------------|
| Logs (non-PII) | Centralized logging (ELK/Cloud Logging) | 90 days |
| Application data (internal) | Managed DB (Cloud SQL) | 1 year |
| Customer PII | Encrypted object store with KMS | As per contract / regulatory requirement |

Retention and deletion:
- Teams must publish retention requirements at service onboarding.
- Automated retention jobs should archive or delete data per policy. Data deletion must be logged and verifiable.

Backups and recovery:
- Critical services: point-in-time backups with daily snapshots and 30-day retention. Recovery RTO/RPO targets must be defined in the service SLOs.

Data sharing and export:
- Exports of Confidential or Restricted data require a documented business justification and approval from Security and Legal.

5) Procurement & expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- Low-cost purchases (< $1,000): Team lead approval.
- Mid-level purchases ($1,000 – $25,000): Manager + Finance approval.
- High-value purchases (> $25,000): Finance + Legal + VP-level approval; multi-year contracts require Executive sponsorship.

Procurement process (steps):
1. Raise a Purchase Request (PR) using the Procurement template; include cost center, business justification, and supplier info.
2. Finance verifies budget and routes for approval.
3. Legal reviews contract terms for vendors above $5,000 or where data processing is involved.
4. Supplier onboarding: complete vendor security questionnaire (see Vendor Management) and enter contract into contract repository.
5. Finance issues PO and tracks delivery.

Expenses and reimbursements:
- Employees should use the company expense system within 30 days of expenditure. Itemized receipts required for all reimbursements.
- Per diem for domestic travel: $75/day; international per diem varies by country (use travel template).
- Corporate card use: limited to pre-approved business expenses; reconciled monthly by cardholder and manager.

Travel booking & safety notes:
- Use the approved travel booking portal (preferred vendors are listed in the Travel template).
- Employees traveling to high-risk regions must register travel with People Ops and complete a short safety briefing.

6) Vendor management

Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Business sponsor identifies vendor and completes Vendor Intake form.
2. Security runs a questionnaire and risk assessment (for vendors with system/data access).
3. Legal negotiates and signs contract (include required security and privacy addenda when handling customer data).
4. Finance and Procurement add vendor to payment system and assign spend limits.
5. Operational onboarding and runbook handoff to team owners.

Vendor monitoring:
- Annual security re-assessment for vendors classified as high or medium risk.
- SLAs and performance metrics documented in contracts; default remediation steps and escalation contacts must be available.

Termination and offboarding vendors:
- Revoke all technical access, collect or destroy any shared data per contract, and maintain evidence of termination.

7) Travel policies (expanded)

Booking and approvals:
- Domestic travel: Manager approval required.
- International travel: Manager + People Ops approval; ensure passport/visa validity and registration for safety notifications.
- Travel to Restricted or high-risk countries requires C-level approval and pre-trip security review.

Allowable expenses:
- Airfare: economy for flights <= 6 hours; premium economy or business only with VP approval for flights > 6 hours.
- Lodging: standard business hotels; nightly rate caps depend on city (see Travel template).
- Meals: reimbursable with itemized receipts; per diem applies where appropriate.

Safety and incident reporting:
- Report any travel incident (health, security, legal) to People Ops and Security within 24 hours.

8) Internal templates and artifacts

Canonical templates (available in /confluence/templates):
- Access Request (access-request-template)
- Change Request (cr-template)
- Procurement / Purchase Request (pr-template)
- Vendor Intake & Security Questionnaire (vendor-intake-template)
- Travel Request & Expense Template (travel-expense-template)
- Onboarding / Offboarding checklist (onboard-offboard-template)

Example: Access Request checklist (abbreviated)
1. Employee name, role, team
2. Systems required (Jira, GitHub, GCP project names)
3. Justification
4. Manager approval (name + timestamp)
5. Data owner approval (if access to Confidential/Restricted data)

9) Exceptions and risk acceptance

- Any deviation from policy must be recorded as a formal exception request with a defined owner, compensating controls, and an expiry date.
- Exceptions for security-sensitive items require Security and CISO approval.

10) Compliance, audit, and metrics

- Quarterly audits: Security & People Ops run quarterly checks on access attestations, vendor assessments, and procurement exceptions.
- Key metrics to track: time-to-provision (target: <2 business days), offboard completion time (target: <4 hours for terminations), number of privileged accounts reviewed quarterly, number of procurement exceptions.

11) Change log and governance

- This document owner is People Ops; Security and Finance are co-owners for enforcement of access, data, and procurement sections.
- Governance cadence: monthly policy sync and quarterly policy review cycle.

Appendix: Contacts & escalation

- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security: security@redwood.ai
- Finance / Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai
- IT/Platform: infra-ops@redwood.ai
